stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab: Rains shut Chhattisgarh schools; 13 MP districts on heavy rain alert
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: Rains shut Chhattisgarh schools; 13 MP districts on heavy rain alert
stories.summary: Heavy rain has shut schools across Chhattisgarh and put riverside villages on flood alert, while the IMD has warned of very heavy rain in 13 Madhya Pradesh districts.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: - Chhattisgarh has closed all government, private and aided schools on Saturday amid heavy rain and flooding concerns.
- Water releases from the Gangrel Dam have raised the alert for villages along the Mahanadi.
- The IMD has warned of very heavy rain in 13 Madhya Pradesh districts as a depression moves towards Uttar Pradesh.
Heavy rain has disrupted travel across parts of Chhattisgarh, prompting a statewide school holiday on Saturday and flood alerts for riverside villages.
In neighbouring Madhya Pradesh, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned of very heavy rain in 13 districts.
Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai ordered all government, private and aided schools to remain closed on 26 September.
He urged parents to keep children at home and directed district administrations to stay ready for relief and rescue work.
Rain has submerged roads and affected connections between districts, particularly in Bastar and adjoining areas.
In Mahasamund, rising water in the Mahanadi and releases from the Gangrel Dam have put 18 riverside villages on alert.
Two guards stranded by floodwater at a liquor shop in Bamhani village were rescued.
All 14 gates of the Gangrel Dam in Dhamtari have been opened as the reservoir filled following sustained rain.
The additional discharge has increased concern for settlements downstream.

stories.headline: Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu orders urgent relief measures in flood-hit areas
stories.title: Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu orders urgent relief measures in flood-hit areas
stories.summary: The Chief Minister directs officials to expedite the process of restoration of power supply, distribute 50 kg of rice to each fisherfolk family, and evolve plans to construct two barrages, one upstream and another downstream of Prakasam Barrage, to impound local floodwaters
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Saturday told the officials to expedite the process of restoration of power supply in the areas that received heavy rains due to the deep depression in the Bay of Bengal and to distribute 50 kg of rice free of cost to each one of the fisherfolk families who could not venture into the sea for the last five days.

Taking stock of the situation in a teleconference along with Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu and Chief Secretary G. Sai Prasad and other senior officials, Mr. Naidu said Vamsadhara water should be diverted into the Hiramandalam reservoir to utilise the floodwaters to the extent possible.

He ordered that relief measures be taken urgently in the waterlogged areas and steps initiated to assess the loss incurred by the agriculture sector so that compensation could be paid with contribution from the Central government.

The Chief Minister ordered that reservoirs across the State be filled with rainwater and called for plans to construct two barrages, one upstream and one downstream of Prakasam Barrage, to impound the local floodwaters and they be sent to the Centre for approval.
The officials told Mr. Naidu that there were no inflows into the Krishna and the rise in water level at Prakasam Barrage was due to the local floods.
Officials explained that the overall rainfall deficit dropped from 50% to 31% due to recent rains.
Coastal Andhra had 19.80% deficit while Rayalaseema 42% deficit.
Though rains subsided for now, river inflows from upstream areas in North Andhra continued, they said.

This comes amid the ongoing row over reports of “illegal” decisions and dissent within the poll body.
The declaration attached to Form 6 would have to be filled out only during the SIR exercise, the ECI said, adding that the earlier format would be applicable otherwise for fresh voter registration.
Those electors who are “unmapped” or have been flagged for “logical discrepancy” will not be issued notices for hearings, the poll panel said.

stories.headline: Invoking Article 142, SC orders reinstatement of former IAF woman officer whose husband died in MiG-21 jet crash
stories.title: Invoking Article 142, SC orders reinstatement of former IAF woman officer whose husband died in MiG-21 jet crash
stories.summary: New Delhi : Exercising its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court has ordered the reinstatement of a former Short Service Commissioned woman officer of the Indian Air Force who had left service in 2013 and later became a war widow after the death of her husband in a MiG-21 fighter jet […] The post Invoking Article 142, SC orders reinstatement of former IAF woman officer whose husband died in MiG-21 jet crash appeared first on KalingaTV .
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Under Article 142, the Supreme Court has ordered the reinstatement of a former Short Service Commissioned woman officer of the Indian Air Force.

New Delhi: Exercising its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court has ordered the reinstatement of a former Short Service Commissioned woman officer of the Indian Air Force who had left service in 2013 and later became a war widow after the death of her husband in a MiG-21 fighter jet crash in 2021.

A Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant allowed the appeal filed by former IAF officer Squadron Leader Priyanka Saxena against orders of the Armed Forces Tribunal, Principal Bench, New Delhi, in 2024 and directed that the Government of India case be treated as a single case without creating any precedent, as it was “very peculiar”.
Article 142 of the Constitution grants the Supreme Court the power to pass any order necessary to secure complete justice.

Squadron Leader Saxena was commissioned in 2003 and stated her unwillingness to seek an extension of service or permanent commission due to family commitments to support her husband, a fighter pilot, and to look after their child.
She left service after completing her 10-year SSC tenure in December 2013.
Her husband, who was with 51 Squadron in Srinagar, died in a MiG-21 Bison crash near Jaisalmer airfield on December 24, 2021.
Following his death, Saxena submitted several applications for reinstatement, citing her 10 years of past service as a Logistics Branch officer.
The plea was rejected by the Indian Air Force, citing government policy, after which she approached the Armed Forces Tribunal seeking quashing of the rejection orders.

She argued that as a former woman officer who had become a widow of a defence personnel, she deserved age relaxation, and that the absence of a policy for such a category could not be a ground to reject her case.

The plea was contested by the government, saying that she had given up her claim for continuation in 2013, her rights had ceased, and she had crossed the maximum age of 35 years fixed under a policy letter dated November 30, 2017, for induction of widows of armed forces personnel.
The Tribunal closed the compliance proceedings on July 2, 2024.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Dismisses BJP MLAs' Plea Challenging Quashing Of Corruption Complaint Against Karnataka Energy Minister KJ George
stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses BJP MLAs' Plea Challenging Quashing Of Corruption Complaint Against Karnataka Energy Minister KJ George
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (25 September) dismissed a Special Leave Petition (SLP) against the Karnataka High Court's judgment which had quashed criminal complaint against Karnataka's Energy Minister KJ George and Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (BESCOM) officials over alleged irregularities in the tender procurement and installation of smart electricity meters in Karnataka.

A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran declined to interfere with the High Court's order, holding that there existed “no good ground to interfere with the impugned order passed by the High Court.”

A criminal complaint was filed against Minister KJ George and BESCOM officials, by three MLAs (CN Ashwath Narayan, SR Vishwanath, and Dheeraj Muniraj) of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), alleging offences under Sections 314, 316, and 61 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), and Section 13(1)(a), 13(1)(b) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (PC Act), in connection with the tender for smart meters.
The MLAs had first approached the Lokayukta police before filing the complaint before the PC Act Special Court.

On George's petition seeking quashing of the proceedings, the Karnataka High Court had quashed the proceedings reasoning that it had found no material to substantiate the corruption allegation, and no allegation of any pecuniary benefit having been received by the Minister.
Aggrieved by the High Court's ruling, the BJP MLAs filed an SLP before the Supreme Court.
“Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and having gone through the materials on record, we find no good ground to interfere with the impugned order passed by the High Court.”
For Petitioners: Mr. Lakshmy Iyenger, Sr. Adv.; Mr. Dhawesh Pahuja, AOR; Mr. Saket Gogia, Adv.; Mr. Aakash Vt, Adv.; Mr. Harshith S, Adv.; Ms. Gauri Pande, Adv.; Mr. Mansingh, Adv.
Mr. Deepesh Meena, Adv.; Mr. Adithya KS, Adv.; Ms. Harshita Singh Tomar, Adv.
For Respondents: Mr. Kapil Sibal, Sr. Adv.; Mr. Vivek Jain, AOR; Ms. Suchitra Kumbhat, Adv.
Mr. Rohit H Nair, Adv.; Ms. Ishika Gandhi, Adv.; Mr. Shathabish Shivanna, Adv.; Mr. Abhishek Janardhan, Adv.; Mr. Samrudh Suraj Hegde, Adv.

stories.headline: Maharashtra declares 265 of 358 talukas drought-hit, announces relief
stories.title: Maharashtra declares 265 of 358 talukas drought-hit, announces relief
stories.summary: The Maharashtra government on Saturday declared 265 of the 358 talukas in the state as drought-affected, announcing relief measures, including restructuring of crop loans, concession in land revenue and deferment of recovery of agriculture-related loans. According to a government resolution issued late on Friday, this covers 74 per cent of the state. The decision follows Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis's recent visit to some drought-affected parts of the state. The state government has activated 'Trigger-1' under its manual for drought management 2016 (updated in 2020) and Drought Management Code to declare drought conditions and initiate relief. Trigger-1 is the first stage in the state's drought framework, activated by a rainfall deficit of more than 25 per cent combined with a prolonged dry spell of 21 days.
